Judgment

The common judgment and award dated 18.04.2019 passed by the reference Court in LAC.Nos.1/2018, 2/2018 and 3/2018 is called in question in these appeals preferred by the beneficiary as well as by the claimants.
02. The reference Court has held that the claimants in all the cases are entitled for an enhanced compensation amount of Rs.142/- per Sq.ft., for the acquired lands along with all statutory benefits.

03. The beneficiary has sought to set aside the reference Court judgment and award and to restore the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer, whereas the claimants have sought to enhance the Shivakumar S/O Annappa Tengli vs The State And Ors on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189098627/
7 compensation by modifying the judgment and award passed by the reference Court.

sentences.text:
The lands of the claimants which are acquired pertain to Sy.No.164/B measuring 01 acre each,
situated at Kapanoor village Tq: and Dist: Kalaburagi, for the purpose of formation of industries under Third Face of Karnataka Industrial Development Board.

The reference Court observing that the lands in question are situated within the city limits of Kalaburagi coming under the GDA area and also noticing that there is much development surrounding the said lands and following the fixation of market value in LAC.No.639/2012 and in LAC.No.413/2013 connected with LAC.No.417/2013 and LAC.No.421/2013 has determined the market value, since the lands in question were situated in the same village and acquired for the same purpose.

05. It is brought to the notice of the Court that in the matter arising out of the above mentioned cases, the beneficiary/Board as well as the claimants approached this Court in MFA.No.201979/2015 and connected matters.

The - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6454-DB Division Bench of this Court vide judgment dated 07.12.2020 was pleased to allow the appeals filed by the Board and set-aside the judgment of the Reference Court and remitted the matters to the reference Court for a decision afresh to be passed strictly in consonance with the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Hargovinddas vs Special Land Acquisition Officer, reported in (1988) 3 SCC 751, Union of India vs.
Dyagala Devamma reported in (2018) 8 SCC 485 and Manoj kumar and others vs. State of Haryana and others reported in (2018) 13 SCC 96 within a period of 06 months from the date of receipt of copy of the order.
06.

Dyagala Devamma reported in (2018) 8 SCC 485

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for the Board submits that following the above judgments, this Court has disposed of a similar appeal filed by the Board in MFA.No.200420/2020 (LAC) by an order dated 19.06.2023, on the same terms.

It is not in dispute that the judgment dated 07.12.2020 passed by this Court in MFA.No.201979/2015 and connected matters, are challenged before the Hon'ble Supreme Court by the claimants, in Special Leave to Appeal (C) No(s).18815-18820/2021 tagged with SPL(C)
No.20233/2021.
In those cases, there was an interim order passed by this Court permitting the claimants to withdraw the amount deposited by the Board.
Insofar as the direction issued for recovery of the amount from the claimants, pursuant to the order passed by this Court, has been stayed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

Shivakumar S/O Annappa Tengli vs The State And Ors on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189098627/
8 08.

In the light of the above interim order passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, this Court in MFA.No.200420/2020 has observed while disposing of the said appeal that, the directions to refund may be deferred for the present and made subject to the outcome in the SLP.(C).No.20233/2021, which is filed against the directions to refund the amount.

It is ordered that the - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6454-DB recovery of the amount deposited by the claimants must be subject to the outcome after remand and final orders in SLP.(C).No.20233/2021.
09.

It is submitted by the learned counsel appearing for the claimants that except the three claimants herein, who have filed the cross-objections, all other claimants have withdrawn the amount deposited by the Board and therefore, he has filed applications to withdraw 25% of the amount in each cases, which has been deposited by the Board.
The said submission is not disputed.
10. We are therefore, of the view that the claimants herein are also entitled to withdraw the amount in deposit.

Hence, it is just and necessary to meet the ends of justice to permit them to withdraw the amount which is however, subject to the outcome of the order passed in SLP.(C).No.20233/2021 and other connected matters.
Learned counsel for the claimants would also contend that the claimants are entitled for higher compensation then what has been awarded by the Reference Court, as it is done in similar other cases.

However, in the light of the orders passed in MFA No.201979/2015 along with connected matters and also in MFA No.200420/2020, the cases on hand have to be remitted back to the reference Court for reconsideration.
It is always open for the claimants to raise all contentions before the Reference Court.

12. For the foregoing reasons, we pass the following;
ORDER I.
All the MFAs and Cross-Objections are allowed.
II. The judgment and award dated 18.04.2019 passed by the Court of Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM, at Kalaburagi in LAC.Nos.1/2018, 2/2018 and 3/2018, are set-aside.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6454-DB III. The appellants / cross-objectors are entitled for the refund of the admissible Court fees.

IV. The matter is remitted back to the Reference Court for fresh disposal in the light of the order passed by this Court in MFA.No.201979/2015 and connected matters disposed of on 07.12.2020 and subject to the outcome of the SLP.(C).No.20233/2021 and connected cases.

9 V.
The claimants are permitted to withdraw the amount which is in deposit before the Reference Court.
The recovery of the amount shall be subject to the final orders in SLP.(C).No.20233/2021 and connected cases.
VI. All the contentions of both the parties are kept open.
VII. The parties shall appear before the reference Court, without further notice on 11.09.2023.
- 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6454-DB VIII.

Pending I.A's if any are disposed of.

Judgment
The common judgment and award dated 18.04.2019 passed by the reference Court in LAC.Nos.1/2018, 2/2018 and 3/2018 is called in question in these appeals preferred by the beneficiary as well as by the claimants.
opennyai_summary.facts:
02. The reference Court has held that the claimants in all the cases are entitled for an enhanced compensation amount of Rs.142/- per Sq.ft., for the acquired lands along with all statutory benefits.
The - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6454-DB Division Bench of this Court vide judgment dated 07.12.2020 was pleased to allow the appeals filed by the Board and set-aside the judgment of the Reference Court and remitted the matters to the reference Court for a decision afresh to be passed strictly in consonance with the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Hargovinddas vs Special Land Acquisition Officer, reported in (1988) 3 SCC 751, Union of India vs.
Dyagala Devamma reported in (2018) 8 SCC 485 and Manoj kumar and others vs. State of Haryana and others reported in (2018) 13 SCC 96 within a period of 06 months from the date of receipt of copy of the order.
06.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In those cases, there was an interim order passed by this Court permitting the claimants to withdraw the amount deposited by the Board.
Insofar as the direction issued for recovery of the amount from the claimants, pursuant to the order passed by this Court, has been stayed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
10. We are therefore, of the view that the claimants herein are also entitled to withdraw the amount in deposit.
Hence, it is just and necessary to meet the ends of justice to permit them to withdraw the amount which is however, subject to the outcome of the order passed in SLP.(C).No.20233/2021 and other connected matters.
opennyai_summary.decision:
However, in the light of the orders passed in MFA No.201979/2015 along with connected matters and also in MFA No.200420/2020, the cases on hand have to be remitted back to the reference Court for reconsideration.
It is always open for the claimants to raise all contentions before the Reference Court.
12. For the foregoing reasons, we pass the following;
ORDER I.
All the MFAs and Cross-Objections are allowed.
II. The judgment and award dated 18.04.2019 passed by the Court of Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM, at Kalaburagi in LAC.Nos.1/2018, 2/2018 and 3/2018, are set-aside.
- 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6454-DB III. The appellants / cross-objectors are entitled for the refund of the admissible Court fees.
IV. The matter is remitted back to the Reference Court for fresh disposal in the light of the order passed by this Court in MFA.No.201979/2015 and connected matters disposed of on 07.12.2020 and subject to the outcome of the SLP.(C).No.20233/2021 and connected cases.
The claimants are permitted to withdraw the amount which is in deposit before the Reference Court.
The recovery of the amount shall be subject to the final orders in SLP.(C).No.20233/2021 and connected cases.
VI. All the contentions of both the parties are kept open.
VII. The parties shall appear before the reference Court, without further notice on 11.09.2023.
